Retrieviewer

일하는 화면에, 작은 친구 하나.

직접 만나 보기 · English · npm · 피드백

앱 창 위에서 혼자 걷고, 뛰고, 앉아서 쉬는 보송한 점자 도트 리트리버예요. 옆잠, 발라당, 몸 말기, 앞발에 턱 괴기. 조용하면 양쪽으로 누워 잠들어요. 가끔 공·간식·터그로 놀아주세요. 가끔 찾아오는 나비를 쫓기도 해요. 나머지 시간에는 각자의 일을 하면 돼요. [BiteFoundry](https://github.com/BiteFoundry)가 만듭니다. 런타임에는 계정, 모델 API, 텔레메트리가 필요하지 않아요. ## 데려오기 **앱 화면이 보이는 컴퓨터**의 터미널에서 실행하세요. Node.js/npm이 없다면 [먼저 설치](PREREQUISITES.md)해 주세요. 1. 설치 또는 업데이트: ```sh npm install -g @bitefoundry/retrieviewer@latest ``` 2. 실행한 뒤, 선택창에서 강아지를 붙일 앱 창을 고르세요. ```sh retrieviewer desktop ``` 다음부터는 `retrieviewer desktop`만 실행하면 돼요. 앱을 개조하거나 MCP로 그림을 주입하지 않아요. 별도의 투명 네이티브 창으로 따라다니며 일반 클릭은 통과시킵니다. 앱 창 단위로 동작하고, 대상 창이 비활성화·최소화되면 숨습니다. 자동 시작이나 셸 래퍼는 등록하지 않아요. 도트 색은 실행할 때 고를 수 있어요. 기본은 크림색이고, 골드색은 `retrieviewer desktop --ink gold`, 밝은 배경에는 `retrieviewer desktop --ink dark`를 쓰세요. 실행 중이라면 먼저 종료하고 다시 실행하세요. 같은 도트에 색만 바꿉니다. `--return-style auto|brake|trot|run-trot`로 귀환도 고를 수 있어요. 기본 `auto`는 기존 제동·총총·달리다 총총을 섞고 같은 동작이 연달아 나오지 않게 합니다. 기존 제동만 쓰려면 `retrieviewer desktop --return-style brake`. 실행 중인 강아지는 직접 종료한 뒤 다시 실행하세요. import해서 쓸 때는 `createPet({returnStyle:'auto'})` 또는 `pet.setReturnStyle('brake')`로 고릅니다. 바꾸면 다음 공놀이부터 적용돼요. > **Cursor / VS Code Remote SSH 사용자:** 원격 서버의 터미널이 아닌, > Cursor 화면이 떠 있는 **로컬 PC의 PowerShell/터미널**에 설치하세요. > 서버의 `DISPLAY=:1`은 서버 쪽 X11 화면을 뜻합니다. VNC로 그 화면을 보고 > 있다면 그 안에서 쓸 수 있지만, 로컬 Cursor 창에 자동으로 붙는 것은 아니에요.
npx로 한 번 써보기 / 명령을 찾을 수 없을 때 ```sh npx --yes --package @bitefoundry/retrieviewer@latest retrieviewer desktop ``` `npx`는 영구 명령 등록이 아니에요. 이후 짧은 명령으로 실행하려면 위의 전역 설치를 해주세요. 전역 설치 후에도 command not found라면 npm 실행 경로를 PATH에 넣어야 해요. [bash·csh/tcsh·Windows별 안내](PREREQUISITES.md#command-not-found). 무조건 sudo npm으로 해결하지 마세요.
## Node.js가 없다면 - **Windows:** [공식 Node.js 설치 페이지](https://nodejs.org/en/download)의 Windows 설치 파일을 쓰세요. npm·PATH 추가 옵션을 유지하고 PowerShell을 새로 여세요. - **macOS:** 같은 공식 페이지의 macOS 설치 파일을 쓰세요. 다만 강아지의 macOS 오버레이는 아직 실기 검증 전인 실험적 지원이에요. - **AlmaLinux8:** 관리자와 Node22 모듈 사용을 확인하세요. 기존 Node 스트림이 없는 환경이라면 `sudo dnf module install nodejs:22`를 사용할 수 있어요. 회사 관리 환경의 모듈을 임의로 reset하거나 바꾸지 마세요. - `node --version`, `npm --version`으로 확인하세요. 패키지는 Node20+를 요구하고, Alma8에서는 Node22.23.4를 검증했어요. [자세한 의존 도구·PATH 안내](PREREQUISITES.md). ## 지원 환경 | 환경 | 상태와 필요 조건 | | --- | --- | | Windows10/11 x64 | 실제 실행 검증. Node20+. 기본 실행은 포함된 네이티브 엔진, 선택형 감시는 .NET 호환 엔진. | | Linux X11 | AlmaLinux8 / GLIBC2.28 / Python3.6.8 / Node22.23.4를 격리된 GUI에서 검증. Python3.6+, X11/Xrender/Xext, compositor 필요. | | macOS | **실험적 지원. 실제 Mac 실행 미검증.** 기본 osascript/AppKit 사용. | | 네이티브 Wayland·화면 없는 SSH | 데스크톱 오버레이 미지원. 세션·보안 설정을 자동 변경하지 않아요. | Linux는 저사양 기본값인 16px 셀·15fps, Windows는 8px 셀·30fps여서 Linux의 점이 더 거칠게 보일 수 있어요. 그림 원본은 같은 Q5 자산입니다. 0.0.21 npm 압축본은 21.42 MB (20.43 MiB)예요. [메모리 측정 기록](PUPPY-MEMORY.md) · [지원 범위와 검증 내용](DESKTOP-PLATFORMS.md). ## 쉽게 종료하고 제거하기 컨트롤에서 종료하거나 `retrieviewer desktop-stop`을 실행하세요. 자체 캐시와 패키지를 제거하려면: ```sh retrieviewer desktop-remove --yes npm uninstall -g @bitefoundry/retrieviewer ``` 데스크톱 동반자는 에이전트 인증정보·실행 파일·셸 프로필을 수정하지 않아요. 별도로 [OpenCode 네이티브 등록](INSTALLING.md)을 했다면 해당 등록을 disconnect한 뒤 제거하세요. Codex/Claude/Cursor 등에 MCP만 연결해 내부 그림을 띄우는 기능은 없어요. ## StackBite 알림 [승인·입력 대기 알림](ATTENTION.md)을 선택해서 켤 수 있어요. 화면 캡처나 다른 앱 조작이나 자동 승인 없이 현재 Room의 메타데이터를 읽어요. 선택형 [유료 DeepSeek/OpenRouter 연결](BRAIN.md)은 익명 이벤트 메타데이터를 판단하며, 기본 규칙은 확인된 대기 알림을 유지해요. LLM을 기다리지 않고 알리며, Windows에 Seat 이름과 대기 종류를 표시해요. 이름은 모델 입력에 들어가지 않아요. 강아지는 가까이 와서 알림 방향을 보고, 앞발로 살살 부르기와 두 발로 서서 벽 박박 긁기를 번갈아 보여줘요. 홈페이지에서도 두 동작을 눌러볼 수 있어요. Windows에서는 npm PowerShell 실행기로 실행하는 StackBite도 감시할 수 있어요. 작업 완료 체크표시는 아직 알림 대상이 아니에요. 업데이트 후, 화면이 보이는 PC의 실행 중인 StackBite Seat에서 실행하세요. ```sh retrieviewer desktop --watch stackbite --brain openrouter ``` [유료 DeepSeek 연결](BRAIN.md)에는 같은 터미널의 `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`가 필요해요. `--brain openrouter`를 빼면 API 없이 규칙 알림만 써요. 이미 실행 중이면 먼저 `retrieviewer desktop-stop`으로 종료하세요. 설치된 `retrieviewer` 명령은 어느 폴더에서든 쓸 수 있어요. `node retrieviewer-cli.mjs`는 소스 폴더 안에서만 쓰는 개발용 명령이에요. ## 직접 만든 TUI에 붙이기 JS 플러그인과 JSONL 브리지를 제공해요. 화면·입력·시간 제어는 호스트가 소유합니다. # Linux X11 companion painter (implementation-ready, not release-certified)

`overlay.py` is the Linux counterpart of `../windows-overlay/Overlay.cs`: a
native transparent painter driven over the same NDJSON stdin/stdout bridge by the
Node pet engine. It draws only the Braille frames it receives; it adds no art.

## Why Python + ctypes

- Python 3.6+ **standard library only**. `ctypes` binds the X client libraries
  the desktop already ships: `libX11.so.6`, `libXrender.so.1`, `libXext.so.6`.
- No compiler, PyPI package, GTK/Qt/gi/Tk, Electron or npm native addon, so there
  is no GLIBC/Node ABI coupling. Target baseline: AlmaLinux 8 (GLIBC 2.28,
  platform Python 3.6) on old hardware.
- Struct layouts and constants were checked against the official X.org headers
  (libX11 1.8.13, libXrender 0.9.12, libXext 1.3.4, xorgproto 2025.1) with a
  compiled `offsetof`/`sizeof` probe on x86_64. 32-bit layouts were not
  compiled; every field uses `c_long`/`c_ulong`/pointers so they follow the C ABI.

## Requirements and refusals (fail closed, one JSON `error` line, exit 2)

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` set or `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland` (even with `DISPLAY`/XWayland) | Refused: log in to an Xorg session. Wayland cannot safely follow/stack over another app. |
| `DISPLAY` unset / display cannot be opened | Refused with the display name. |
| No SHAPE ≥ 1.1 (input shapes), no RENDER, no XRender ARGB32 32-bit visual | Refused. |
| No compositing manager (`_NET_WM_CM_Sn` unowned) | Refused instead of painting an opaque black box. |
| WM without EWMH `_NET_CLIENT_LIST` / `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW` | Refused. |
| Missing X client library | Refused; it never installs packages. |

## Bridge (same as Windows)

stdin: `frame{revision,x,y,columns,rows,text}`, `loaded`, `interaction`, `error`, `quit`.
stdout: `ready{pickerVisible}`, `picker{visible}`,
`viewport{revision,visible,selected,columns,rows,cellWidth,cellHeight=2*cellWidth}`,
`ack{painted}`, `interact{kind:ball|treat}`, `pause{paused}`, `quit`.

- One outstanding frame; discarded, hidden and stale-revision frames are still ACKed.
- Only U+2800..U+28FF cells; ≤ 125000 cells per frame. Default cell is 16 px and the
  viewport grid is capped at 20000 cells (`--cell 6|8|10|12|16` to change the cell).
- Only the cropped bounding box is rasterized; the pet window is resized to it and
  fully overwritten, and is unmapped on every viewport change, so no stale trails.
- stdin EOF quits; every owned window, GC and colormap is released and the display
  connection closed. The single-instance lock is an abstract Unix socket (no file).

## Window behavior

- Explicit picker lists EWMH client windows (title and `/proc/PID/comm` only,
  terminals first). Titles are drawn ASCII-only (`?` for other characters).
  The picker sets `WM_HINTS.input=False` so the WM should not move keyboard focus.
- Tracking is read-only polling (~30 Hz) of the target's attributes, root-relative
  position, `_NET_WM_STATE_HIDDEN`, `_NET_WM_PID` and `_NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW`. The pet
  shows only while the target is the active window, viewable, not minimized and at
  least 160×120. A vanished target (BadWindow is trapped) or reused PID hides it.
- Pet: override-redirect ARGB32 window with an **empty ShapeInput region**, so all
  pointer input passes through; no keyboard selection, grabs or hotkeys.
- Controls: a separate override-redirect strip (Ball, Treat, Window, Pause, Quit)
  consumes only its own clicks and is never focused.
- Target windows and global focus are never modified. No capture, injection,
  network, root access or Wayland compositor changes.

## Commands

```sh
python3 overlay.py                  # bridge mode (spawned by the Node worker)
python3 overlay.py --ipc-test       # bridge mode with an owned off-screen stand-in target
python3 overlay.py --check-json     # environment diagnostics, creates no windows
python3 overlay.py --self-test :99  # owned windows on an explicitly named isolated display (e.g. Xvfb)
```

`--self-test` refuses an implicit display; it does not require a compositor and
checks painting, input-shape emptiness, geometry following, stale-frame discard,
hide on unmap, target loss, focus preservation and teardown on owned windows only.

## Known limits

- Parent verification after the worker report: AlmaLinux8/GLIBC2.28, Python3.6.8,
  Node22.23.4, owned Xvfb + Openbox + xcompmgr passed native painting, empty input
  shape, focus/geometry/hide/stale-frame checks and real Node worker ball/exit
  lifecycle. This is not certification of every physical desktop/compositor.
- Compositors may draw a shadow around override-redirect windows; the pet window
  declares `_NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE_DND`, which most compositors leave unshadowed.
- The overlay is raised every 250 ms while visible because a WM restacks the active
  target above override-redirect windows when it is clicked.

# macOS transparent companion helper (JXA)

`overlay.jxa` is the macOS painter for the existing Node Braille pet engine. It is
the macOS counterpart of `integrations/windows-overlay/Overlay.cs` and speaks the
same NDJSON protocol (`integrations/windows-overlay/protocol.mjs`).

It runs with the interpreter that ships with macOS:

```sh
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript integrations/macos-overlay/overlay.jxa            # companion
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript integrations/macos-overlay/overlay.jxa --ipc-test # owned off-screen target
/usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript integrations/macos-overlay/overlay.jxa --self-test [proof.tiff]
```

No Xcode, Swift compiler, Homebrew, Python, Electron or downloaded binary is
needed. The helper uses JavaScript for Automation's ObjC bridge to AppKit,
Foundation and CoreGraphics only. The Node launcher (owned by the main package)
spawns it with an argv array (never a shell string). Setup is still two steps:
`npm install -g @bitefoundry/retrieviewer` and then `retrieviewer desktop`.

## What it does and does not touch

- **Reads only window metadata**: `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` (id, owner PID/name,
  bounds, layer, on-screen flag and the title when macOS allows it) plus
  `NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication`. It never captures screen pixels. It does not
  use the Accessibility API, event taps, global monitors, AppleScript/System Events,
  injection or terminal/chat content.
- **Never requests or changes privacy settings.** Without Screen Recording
  permission macOS withholds other apps' window titles, so the picker shows
  `App · 창 #<windowID>`. No permission prompt is triggered.
- **Pet**: a borderless `NSPanel` with the `nonactivatingPanel` style. It is clear,
  shadowless and `ignoresMouseEvents = true` (click-through), and it can never become
  key or main. Dots use the Overlay.cs geometry: Braille bit order, half-cell pitch
  and a 0.48 diameter. They are rasterized in JS into one premultiplied RGBA TIFF per
  frame (Retina 2x when it costs no more than ~2M pixels), so each frame needs only
  a few bridge calls.
- **Controls**: a separate non-activating strip with 공 / 간식 / 창 / 쉼 / 종료
  buttons. These buttons accept the first click, so using them does not take focus
  from the terminal. A menu bar item, the counterpart of the Windows tray, offers
  choose window / hide-show / quit.
- **Window scope**: it follows the whole selected window's bounds, including its
  title bar, because the content rect of another app needs Accessibility. It does
  not track tabs. It is shown only while the target app is frontmost **and** the
  target is that app's front window. It hides when the window is minimized, the
  app is hidden, the window is on another Space or the picker is open. It drops the
  target when the window closes.
- **Grid**: 12pt cells, or 16pt when a 12pt grid would exceed 20000 cells.
  `cellHeight = 2 × cellWidth` (0.5 aspect). Hard cap 125000 cells.
- **Coordinates**: CG global space (top-left of the primary display, y down) is
  converted to Cocoa (bottom-left, y up) with `y' = H(primary) − (y + h)`. Both
  spaces are in points, so Retina scale and secondary displays with negative
  origins need no special case.

## Runloop and I/O

- stdin: `NSFileHandle readInBackgroundAndNotifyForModes:` reads on Foundation's
  background thread. A registered `NSObject` subclass receives the completion
  notification on the main runloop. Bytes are split on `\n` at the `NSData` level
  before UTF-8 decoding, so multi-byte Braille characters never split. A line is
  capped at 800000 bytes. EOF quits.
- A 50ms `NSTimer` in common modes tracks geometry and focus. Frames paint as soon
  as they arrive. Every frame is acknowledged (`painted:false` when stale or
  hidden).
- `NSApplication run` (accessory policy, no Dock icon) runs the real Cocoa event
  loop. Quitting hides all windows, removes the menu bar item, emits `quit` and
  calls `exit(0)`, so osascript never prints a script result on stdout.
- stdout carries only `JSON.stringify(...) + "\n"` written through
  `NSFileHandle`. There is no `console.log`.

`macos-overlay-helper.test.mjs` runs under Node on any OS. It checks the source
contract: ASCII/ES5-only, no forbidden APIs, wiring of the runloop, stdin and timer,
and panel flags. It also checks the pure code paths, which run unmodified under

After `npm install -g @bitefoundry/retrieviewer@latest`, run from a live StackBite

## What it reads

Only the fixed read-only command `stackbite agent seats --output json`, at most
once every five seconds after the previous read finishes. StackBite revalidates
the inherited caller Seat/generation. The source requires a live Room binding;
launching from an unrelated terminal is refused rather than guessing credentials.

On Windows, a native executable or npm PowerShell launcher is resolved on PATH.

string or execution-policy change. Unix retains the direct command.

## Behavior and limits

Attention now has two authored gestures: a seated gentle paw and a standing
two-hind-foot glass scrabble. Automatic cues alternate; hosts can pass
`gesture:'paw'` or `gesture:'wall'` to `pet.notify`. See [wall motion](ATTENTION-WALL.md)

variant using simulated input; it does not request a real approval.

The ginger cat uses a finite eye greeting for passive alerts. Its current direct
interaction or feeding finishes before the monitor can deliver the greeting.

- A new exact Room/Seat/generation/turn/request cues one connected attention episode:
  brake/recover and face the user, approach using the existing world path if more
  than 0.8 m from the near check-in point, then sit, gently paw the air twice,
  lower the paw and look left. See [paw motion and cost](ATTENTION-PAW.md). Near pets stay
  in place. Resolution during approach brakes the obsolete journey naturally.
  Left means the sidebar direction, not a detected button coordinate.
- The rule cue is accepted before optional inference starts. LLM latency, failure
  or disagreement never delays, repeats or retracts a confirmed pending alert.
  This does not remove the existing five-second source polling interval.
- Explicit ball/treat/tug interactions win. A rejected cue retries only while
  its source fact is fresh. Distinct cues are at least 20 seconds apart.
- Resolved/disconnected/stale facts clear the cue. Source errors are unavailable,
  not “zero pending.” A hidden/paused pet aborts observation and refreshes on resume.
- At most 32 pending items and 128 dedupe identities are retained, in memory only.
  Excess/malformed snapshots fail closed. No unlimited history or recording.
- Each read has a 4-second timeout and 256 KiB output cap. No overlapping reads,
  separate resident watcher, additional timer or shell command interpreter.
  The CLI briefly runs a child process; it is not free in CPU/peak RAM.

## What leaves the PC

Only fixed system instructions and this allowlisted anonymous state:

```json
{"event":"pending_input","kind":"approval","pending_count":1}
```

No Room/Seat/request identifiers, labels, task text, terminal output, screenshots,
clipboard or credentials appear in prompts. The key goes only in the Authorization
header to the fixed HTTPS OpenRouter URL, never to helper or StackBite child

policy leaves no eligible route, it falls back rather than weakening the policy.

## Judgment and fallback

The model may return only `{"decision":"notify"}`, `ignore`, or `uncertain`.
JSON mode is not a correctness guarantee: code rejects extra keys, malformed/
truncated output, tool calls and responses over 32 KiB. No returned text is run,
typed, used as a coordinate, or displayed as a factual summary.

This first connection is **advisory on known pending-input facts**, not screen
understanding. Since 0.0.15, a confirmed approval/question is
delivered by the rule first; optional model work starts only after the pet accepts
the cue. It cannot delay, suppress, repeat or retract the cue. Diagnostics show
`rule_first` while advice is pending, then `model_notify` for agreement,
`rule_override` for disagreement, or `rule_fallback` for uncertain/errors.
The 0.0.14 baseline waited for advice. With only kind/count facts, the model adds little semantic value;
this slice establishes a bounded backend before optional richer perception.

Each accepted exact pending item is judged once while fresh; rejected cues during
direct play do not spend requests. Seat display names stay local. Resolution, generation
replacement, stale source, pause, hide and shutdown cancel its request; late
answers cannot resurrect a notice. Direct ball/treat/tug still wins. Animation
ticks never await HTTP. Network timeout is 3 seconds; a host-tick guard discards
hung advice within 3.5 seconds of active time, without delaying the already-issued
rule alert. `brain-check`
allows 8 seconds for diagnosis, not for normal pet reactions.

## Resource and request limits

- One inference at a time. No automatic network retries or alternate-model fallback.
- Fixed paid model with provider price ceilings of $0.30 per million input tokens
  and $1.20 per million output tokens, with per-request fees disallowed. These are
  unit-price limits, not an account spending cap. Thinking disabled,
  temperature 0, maximum 96 output tokens; no tools or plugins.
- Up to 16 anonymous successful judgments cached for 60 seconds. Same state can
  reuse an answer without another request; source identity/freshness stays local.
- Default 40 HTTP attempts per UTC day **per process lifetime**. Restarts reset
  this guard, and other apps share account limits; it is not a global quota meter.
- A 429 backs off for 60 seconds. Other request failures back off for 10 seconds.
  No new calls while the pet is hidden/paused or the source has no fresh events.
- Requests use bounded transient buffers; the API adds network/HTTP runtime costs.
  No claim of zero RAM overhead or guaranteed endpoint latency is made.

The catalog price on 2026-10-24 was $0.15 input / $0.60 output per million tokens,
with scheduled peak pricing at $0.30 / $1.20. Provider prices vary; the request
ceilings fail closed if no compatible route remains. Check the
[model and provider prices](https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017/providers)
before budgeting. Even an aborted/timed-out request can incur provider usage.

Reference contracts: [OpenRouter parameters](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/parameters),
[provider routing](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection),
[reasoning](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/reasoning-tokens).
The state/closed-choice design follows the TypeSafe skill's guidance, but no

# Embedding Retrieviewer

See [PLUGIN.md](./PLUGIN.md) for the convenience plugin. The headless core has no
timers, DOM, keyboard, output or process listeners. The host owns time/rendering.
createPet reads bundled art; import alone does not. Node >=20, or browser ES modules
with Three resolution and DecompressionStream. No native Python/Rust binding.

```js
import {createPet} from '@bitefoundry/retrieviewer';
const pet = await createPet(); // Q5, 32 levels, all 2,341 source poses retained
// Keep this instance for the whole pane lifetime, not one per frame.
pet.step(elapsedSeconds);
const {text} = pet.frame({columns, rows});
pane.setContent(text);
pet.interact('ball'); // or 'treat'; false when busy/cooling down
// on unmount:
pet.dispose();
```

## Core contract

- createPet({loadAsset?,seed?,energy?,pawTransport?,artProfile?}): default q5.
  Seed uint32, energy 0..1; keep pawTransport enabled.
- step(dt): finite nonnegative seconds, fixed 1/60s simulation. Each call admits
  at most 0.1s to avoid unbounded stalled-host catch-up. Returns step count.
- frame({columns,rows,cellAspect=.5,camera?,poseFps=24,contactEnabled=true}):
  exactly rows lines of columns Unicode Braille characters, no ANSI or trailing
  newline. Positive integer dimensions, at most125,000 cells. Pose cadence12/24/30.
  cellAspect = character width / line height, positive finite.
- Frame contains text,columns,rows,artProfile,pixels,state,report,placement,
  projection,mouth,contacts. pixels is a **borrowed** RGBA buffer: valid only until
  next frame/dispose; copy if retaining. The wrapper also retains no frame.
- needsFrame(frameOptions): optional pre-render check for a host that only needs
  changed pictures. False means a known held pose and all visible objects match
  the last frame. Always keep calling step(dt); needs/cooldowns/autonomy continue.
  Moving poses, gestures, visitors and sleep cues conservatively return true.
  frame() itself never skips or returns stale metadata. Force a frame when the
  host loses its display contents (for example after hiding or reconnecting).
- camera:{viewportWidth,viewportHeight,rect:{left,top,width,height}} places a pane
  within a larger viewport. Keep it consistent across time for metric perspective.
- interact('ball'|'treat'): false while busy/cooling down; unknown kind throws.
- dispose(): idempotent. Every other core method afterwards throws.

Default-loader pets share immutable art, not behavior/clocks/output buffers; last
dispose releases shared assets. Custom loaders are isolated. Initialization is async
I/O with synchronous CPU decode between loads; avoid repeated creation on render.
node examples/embed.mjs [columns] [rows] prints one frame.
npm run pet:companion (installed retrieviewer preview) is the opt-in fullscreen host:
B ball, T treat, Space pause, Q quit. Only that executable owns input/screen.
Redirected stdout prints one plain frame and exits.

## Assets / original option

Default files resolve against the module URL, never cwd (lazy Node fs or browser
HTTP fetch). getPetAssetFiles(profile?) returns 19 filenames: nine art archives
plus ten metadata files. Copy these unchanged for bundlers. The default Q5 files
use `.rvz`, an index followed by individually gzip-compressed crops. A custom
loader returns the original ArrayBuffer/typed bytes, without unpacking the archive.

Local Node hosts using the default loader read only the indices at creation and
read/decode requested crops synchronously into a two-frame cache per family.
There is no background loader or extra process. The final pet's `dispose()` closes
the shared files. Custom loaders and browsers use the portable memory-backed
store; they do not receive the local file-backed memory reduction.

```js
import {createPet,getPetAssetFiles} from '@bitefoundry/retrieviewer';
const files = getPetAssetFiles(); // deploy these files unchanged
const base = new URL('/pets/retrieviewer/', location.origin);
const pet = await createPet({loadAsset: async name => {
  const r = await fetch(new URL(name, base));
  if (!r.ok) throw Error(name + ': HTTP ' + r.status);
  return r.arrayBuffer();
}});
```

Original256-level caches remain in the source workspace. Use
createPet({artProfile:'original'}) there, or ?palette=original in the preview.
They are **not bundled** in the small distribution. For external original art,
copy getPetAssetFiles('original') from the workspace and supply loadAsset. Missing
originals fail clearly, never silently fall back.

Q5 is lossy quantization (max original-source pixel error 4/255). The indexed
repack is lossless relative to the approved Q5 art: all 2,401 logical frames and
their timing remain unchanged. The nine indexed archives total 19,326,068 bytes;
their indices total 54,040 bytes. No Three.js dependency runs in the pet core.
See [PUPPY-MEMORY.md](./PUPPY-MEMORY.md) for measured costs and host limitations.

## JSONL bridge (Python/Rust/other process hosts)

Spawn installed retrieviewer-stdio or node /path/to/retrieviewer-stdio.mjs.
Wait for {"event":"ready","protocol":1}. Send JSON objects one per line; replies echo
optional string/number/null id. Stdout contains only JSONL, never ANSI.
No autonomous clock: your app sends tick at its own cadence.

```json
{"id":1,"op":"tick","dt":0.03333333333333333,"columns":80,"rows":24}
{"id":2,"op":"interact","kind":"ball"}
{"id":3,"op":"dispose"}
```

tick combines step+frame in one round trip; separate step/frame remain supported.
Frame/tick replies: {id,ok:true,text,columns,rows,report,artProfile}; step replies have
steps, interaction replies accepted. Errors: {id,ok:false,error}. A failed tick may
advance time before frame validation; requests are not transactions.
Dispose acknowledges and exits; stdin EOF also disposes. Node remains required.
examples/bridge.py uses only Python's standard library. Each process loads its own
art; reuse one per host, not per frame.

## Recovering an interrupted settings change

Settings writes use an exclusive `settings.lock`. New locks record the owning
PID, hostname, start time and a random token. A busy error prints the exact lock
path and PID when known. An old or empty lock may have no owner information.
Locks are deliberately **not** deleted just because they are old or a PID probe
fails: a long operation, PID reuse or a shared directory can make that unsafe.

If an operation crashed:

1. Stop all Retrieviewer enable/disable/disconnect commands and close all host
   agents that can change its settings. If the directory is shared, stop writers
   on every machine. Inspect the exact lock named in the error; an active owner
   must finish first. Do not kill an unrelated process just because its PID matches.
2. With **all writers stopped**, move only that `settings.lock` aside in the same
   directory (for example to `settings.lock.recovered`). Keep it as a backup;
   do not overwrite an existing backup, touch `settings.json`, remove the whole
   directory, or follow a symlink. Then retry the original command. A fresh lock
   is acquired normally and the existing settings are preserved.

Default directory: `%USERPROFILE%\.config\retrieviewer` on Windows,
`~/.config/retrieviewer` on macOS/Linux. `RETRIEVIEWER_HOME` overrides it, so use
the path in the error rather than assuming the default. This is an **offline
manual recovery**, not a command to remove a live lock or automatic stale reaping.

# Precomputed motion tables (0.0.12)

`npm run bake:motion` compiles the current approved sources into
`puppy-motion-tables.generated.mjs`. It does not change a picture, camera,
trajectory, animation duration or source metadata. `npm run check:motion` checks
the exact deterministic output without writing. Tests and the publication guard
reject stale output after source metadata or witnessed art changes.

## What is precomputed

- Source support episodes, including continuous stance across a cycle seam and
  a complete swing skipped between rendered frames. No stance-history discovery
  occurs while building a default renderer, including after a resize.
- Clip lists, weights and totals used for action-pose addressing. The runtime no
  longer validates/rebuilds these same lists and totals for each default pose.
- A dense table of72 facing/seat preparation cases, sharing8 step descriptors.
  Lookup requires a stationary root; it does not insert a turn at running speed.
- Ten exact-pixel connection witnesses with view, speed and (where applicable)
  gait-phase/velocity-match requirements. These cover walk entry/exit, rear run
  into the authored impact, impact into rear pickup, carry-gather into arrival
  seat, tug into the canonical seat, and four watch endpoints into that seat.
- SHA256 of every input metadata/art file used by the bake. JSON text is hashed
  with LF line endings; binary artwork is hashed byte-for-byte. Generated text
  checks also accept CRLF checkouts. No source images,
  source hashes or graph search are computed by the running pet.

The generated routes preserve the existing approved preparation order. This is
a bounded compilation of existing paths, not unrestricted motion matching or a
new animation blend engine. Other actor-specific recovery rules stay in place.
Unregistered arbitrary-phase joins are not certified: in particular an urgently
interrupted walk may use its existing recovery rather than a proven phase0 join.

## What remains dynamic

World displacement, actual velocity, unwrapped gait phase, perspective and the
small paw-to-world anchor correction still depend on live state. Those cannot
be baked as fixed screen coordinates while allowing free travel and resizing.
Support tables address the original source coordinates; they do not stretch the
head/torso, replace drawings or cause a camera orbit.

Paw labels are visible image-space proxies, not anatomical motion capture. Some
resting endpoints have exact-pose evidence but no individually labeled paws.
The authored run-to-impact entry is **airborne**, not a planted-paw handoff:
its gate requires the correct phase, positive speed and matched velocity.
Neither exact pixels nor a green numerical test proves general animal realism.

## Compatibility and resource scope

The bundled Q5/default-loader path uses the compiled tables. Optional original
art and custom loaders retain the general metadata-driven implementation instead
of accidentally applying the bundled pet's bake to unrelated art. The general
helpers remain available for authoring and equivalence tests.

The generated module is about11KB source, shared between instances; there is no
extra image cache, dependency, timer, worker or asset-fetch round trip. It removes

const puppy = await createPetPlugin({
  host: {
    // Return null while hidden. Use CONTENT size, excluding widget border/padding.
    getSize: () => visible ? {columns: contentWidth, rows: contentHeight} : null,
    render: ({text}) => { widget.setContent(text); screen.render(); },

## Own loop instead of plugin clock

```js
const puppy = await createPetPlugin({host}); // creation does not render/start timers
// existing host frame loop (do NOT also call start):
puppy.tick(elapsedSeconds);
// existing host interaction input:
puppy.interact('ball');
// teardown:
puppy.dispose();
```

`start()` is opt-in scheduling, `pause()` stops scheduling without unloading,
`render()` redraws without advancing, `tick(dt)` advances+draws. `start()` is
idempotent; resume ignores paused wall time. `running`/`disposed` are readable.
Host size is checked each frame; no resize listeners are installed. Hidden/null
or zero-sized panes neither advance nor draw. Disposal cancels scheduling, releases
pet and invokes optional clear once. Direct host errors throw; scheduled errors
pause and invoke onError if supplied (otherwise stay paused). Host callbacks are
synchronous; avoid retaining borrowed frame pixels. See types for custom scheduler.

Source pixel v becomes q=round(v*31/255), displayed as round(q*255/31). Maximum

frames to the existing 8-bit sampler interface. Original and Q5 caches have separate
sharing/refcount entries; pets' actors, needs, clocks and buffers remain independent.

# Windows companion — 0.0.2

This is a separate transparent desktop window, not a Codex plugin or a terminal
wrapper. Version0.0.2 includes it; version0.0.1 does not. Setup is two steps:

1. `npm install -g @bitefoundry/retrieviewer`
2. `retrieviewer desktop` — choose the app window in the picker.

Choose a supported ordinary Windows app window (including a terminal containing
Codex). Then use your app normally, without a
wrapper, shell alias, patched binary, changed credentials, or agent configuration.
Basic mode uses the bundled QuickJS/Win32 engine in one process; Node exits
after launch. No Electron, Chromium, extra npm dependency or compiler is needed.
Windows10/11 x64 with Node20+ is required. Optional watch/brain or --engine node
keeps the existing Node/.NET compatibility path and its Framework4 compiler. Other
desktop platforms and exclusive fullscreen/security surfaces are not certified.
Launch reports
that the picker is ready, **not** that the user has selected a window or visually
approved the pet.

## Interaction and window scope

- The original Q5 Braille artwork/behavior engine is reused without new sprites.
- The pet is click-through and non-activating. It does not read keyboard input.
- A small separate, non-activating control strip offers ball, treat, choose window,
  pause and exit. These buttons consume their own clicks, not terminal typing.
- Ball/treat use the existing engine interactions, including busy/cooldown rules.
  Ball currently uses its existing preset destination, **not free mouse aiming**.
- The overlay follows the selected window's client rectangle. It hides and stops
  simulation when another app is foreground, the target is minimized, or paused.
  The control strip remains available while paused in the selected window.
- It binds a whole top-level window, **not a terminal tab/pane**. Switching tabs
  inside that window does not automatically rebind or identify the running agent.
- Selection is per launch. There is no process scanning to infer Codex sessions,
  screen scraping/OCR, chat capture, global keyboard hook or input injection.
  The picker locally reads window titles/process names; tracking reads window
  geometry, foreground state, visibility and owning process ID.
- No automatic startup, background scheduled task, registry entry or MCP is added.
  Exit stops the native process. The compatibility path stops both painter and engine;
  if either closes, its counterpart exits too. Losing the target hides the pet; tray selection can attach another.

## Stop, remove, and recover

```powershell
retrieviewer desktop-status --json
retrieviewer desktop-stop
retrieviewer desktop-clean --yes
```

One-command companion removal (stop, wait for exit, remove only its cache):

```powershell
retrieviewer desktop-remove --yes
```

The control strip provides window selection, pause/resume and exit. The older
compatibility helper also has a tray menu. `desktop-stop`
asks the companion to exit through an authenticated local named pipe; it never
kills a PID from a stale file. The worker may terminate only its own stuck child
painter after a graceful timeout. Cache cleanup refuses a live/unreachable worker,
symlinks/junctions and unrecognized session records. It removes only recognized
helper cache filenames; unrelated files and agent/pet settings remain untouched.

Own files are under `~/.config/retrieviewer/desktop` (or RETRIEVIEWER_HOME/desktop):
one hash-named compiled helper and a transient local session capability record.
The token is not printed by status and is never sent over a network. Same-user
local software is not treated as an adversarial security boundary. No screenshot,
terminal content or window title is persisted by this companion.

For a globally installed copy, stop/remove the companion before
`npm uninstall -g @bitefoundry/retrieviewer`. Other native OpenCode registrations,
if any, must first be disconnected with the existing explicit disconnect command.
This companion does not change or remove a pre-existing Codex `/pets` pack.

## Rendering and bounded work

Native pixels are dots decoded from the engine's existing Braille cells, on an
alpha-transparent bitmap. Every frame starts clear, avoiding previous-frame paw
trails. Only the nonblank bounding rectangle crosses IPC and is painted; the
native window does not allocate a full-screen transparent bitmap. A request/ack
bridge permits only one frame in flight. Viewport revisions discard frames from
an old size/position; discarded frames are acknowledged to avoid deadlock. Hidden
time is not replayed when the pet becomes visible. The engine targets30fps, but
the actual frame rate depends on CPU, window resolution and Windows scheduling.

## Search-first decision and evidence

Reused `createPet` and its side-effect-free host API. A small native Win32 painter
was selected for Windows instead of adding an Electron runtime or a PTY wrapper.
The former adds another browser runtime; the latter changes how Codex is launched
and was explicitly rejected. This is not a claim of cross-platform support or a
benchmarked memory advantage; measurements belong to the local validation.

- [Layered windows and mouse passthrough](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/window-features#layered-windows)
- [UpdateLayeredWindow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-updatelayeredwindow)
- [No-activate extended window style](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/extended-window-styles)
- [SetWindowPos without activation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowpos)
- [Electron alternative](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/custom-window-interactions)

`node --test retrieviewer-desktop.test.mjs` covers transport/cropping/backpressure,
hidden-time resets, CLI isolation, authenticated control transport and conservative
cleanup. Native validation must additionally test layered window rendering, focus,
geometry, minimize/restore, controls and lifecycle on an actual Windows desktop.
Do not equate style checks or a rendered PNG with end-user visual approval.
